results.title: Connect AI to your wiki through the XWiki MCP Server
results.content:
Right now, for most companies, the answer to your questions already exists somewhere in a wiki. Without linking that data to your AI assistant, you're just begging for hallucinations served with confidence. Your assistant will gladly be of service.

Fixing the data-linking issue has become really easy, though. As long as you're using XWiki as a knowledge base, you can now connect any AI assistant to your wiki through our Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server. You choose whether it's the latest state-of-the-art model or a self-hosted model you want to use with sensitive data. All you need is the XWiki MCP Server Extension and your preferred AI tool. These include: OpenCode, Pi, Codex, Claude Code, some of the millions of Copilots Microsoft has to offer, or any other tool that supports MCP. [...] You now need to run

`` `opencode mcp auth xwiki```

in your terminal, accept the connection, and then you should be set!

Note that by default, the agent can only read content. You'll need to enable write permissions in the MCP configuration.

## Explore what the MCP Server can do with your knowledge

Use the XWiki MCP Server in XWiki Cloud, on your self-hosted instance, or not at all. Connecting AI to your wiki should always be your choice. Everything we've built was built with these principles in mind.

Even in beta, the current version of the XWiki MCP Server extension can already do a lot. You can work with pages, structured data, and attachments, all in natural language, and while using your preferred AI tools. [...] By connecting AI to your wiki through the MCP Server, you can use natural language to do tasks you'd otherwise do manually. Tasks that would normally take you a couple of hours can now be done in a matter of minutes, in the background, while you work on something else. Make sure to check the results, though, and never fully trust the machine!

## Why we built the XWiki MCP Server

When we started thinking about integrating an MCP Server into XWiki, making it optional and self-hostable was the default choice. While useful, AI tools are just that — tools. We believe it is your right to choose whether you want to use these tools, and if you do, in what capacity.
